messages:
morgan: Quick check — after enabling INT8 KV cache on the 70B FP8 baseline job I see memory down ~34% but p99 decode latency up by ~16%. Profile traces look noisy.

sanjay: Can you paste the flame or the perf counters? Did kernel selection flip to the int8 GEMM path?

morgan: Attached snippet from perf (trimmed):
```
KV_WRITE_BYTES: 1.2GB -> 0.8GB
CUDA_MEMCPY_MS: 18.3 -> 21.8
KERNEL:int8_kv_pack: 12.3ms (↑)
KERNEL:fp8_kv_unpack: 9.1ms
```
Looks like int8 packing adds a misaligned load path on our page boundaries — see offsets at 4096/8192.

lina: Misaligned pagewalks? That's the same issue we saw in the TPU sims. Could cause extra kernel invocations on small batches.

priya: Any change in batching heuristics? Small-batch tails could amplify misalignment overhead.

morgan: Yes — batch distribution shifted after we bumped max_tokens_per_request to 1024. Tail batches (<=4 reqs) spiked. Proposed fix: opportunistic coalesce on tails + force fp8 kernels for last N tokens to avoid int8 pack/unpack churn.

ben: Config proposal:
```
{"batching": {"coalesce_tail": true, "coalesce_threshold": 4, "fallback_kernel":"fp8", "tail_saturation_tokens":128}}
```

morgan: Ran canary with that config. Results: mem savings ~30% (vs fp8 baseline), p99 latency regressed only 3% vs baseline (acceptable), decode perplexity unchanged on devset. But we saw token drift on a small subset when using pure int8 KV with no fallback.

priya: Token drift = decode quality degradation?

morgan: Tiny insertion jitter at long prefixes (>1024 tokens) — model more likely to repeat tokens. Not catastrophic but noticeable in rouge/bleu tests.

sanjay: Sounds like calibration error from per-layer int8 quant scales. Did you try per-head vs per-tensor scales?

morgan: Per-head INT8 reduced drift but doubled pack time. Per-tensor is faster but slightly worse quality. Hybrid approach (per-head for last 2 layers + per-tensor elsewhere) gave best tradeoff in canary.

lina: For rollout plan: 1) enable coalesce_tail heuristic, 2) opportunistic kernel fallback to fp8 for small tail/saturation, 3) elective per-head quant on final layers. Monitor p99 and NLL/CTE evals.

dev-bot: Canary deployed to cluster redwood-canary-3 at 1987654326 by morgan. Alert if p99 > 1.15x baseline or NLL delta > 0.02.

ben: I'll add a tracing field for misaligned offsets to perf events so we can correlate page boundaries to kernel overhead.

morgan: Thanks — next step is a broader A/B with traffic split 5/95. I'll open a short runbook and add the sample traces.

priya: :thumbsup: Keep an eye on memory fragmentation — coalescing can backfire if allocation pattern changes.

morgan: noted, will include allocation histograms.
